title: Vulnerable Agent Identification in Large-Scale Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
claim: Our predicted vulnerability scores correlate strongly with the actual reward degradation under attack, across tasks and agent counts.
layout: 2 side-by-side scatter plots with regression lines, Pearson stats in titles
description: Two side-by-side scatter plots with identical styling. The left panel is titled 'Task: Battle, Agent Num 64' and the right is 'Task: Taxi, Agent Num 100'. The x-axis in both is 'Reward Under Attack'. The y-axis is 'Predicted Value', and its label is cut off in the left panel. Each panel has about a dozen salmon-pink dots, a linear regression line, and a shaded confidence band. Both slope upward. Italic bold text under each title reports the Pearson correlation: R=0.97 (p=1.85e-11) for Battle and R=0.91 (p=1.61e-07) for Taxi. Grey gridlines sit behind the points. Several points sit in loose clusters. The eye goes first to the bold titles and Pearson numbers, then to the rising trend line. The figure does not match the caption, which describes darker-is-more-vulnerable heatmaps.
caption: (a,b) Change from $\epsilon^i = 0$ to $\epsilon^i = 1$. Some agents contributes more to overall system when compromised. (c,d) Change from $\xi = 0$ to $\xi = 1/N$. Agents receive more impact when facing attackers. Darker cell indicates higher vulnerability.
abstract: Partial agent failure becomes inevitable when systems scale up, making it crucial to identify the subset of agents whose failure causes worst-case system performance degradations. We study this Vulnerable Agent Identification (VAI) problem in large-scale multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). We frame VAI as a Hierarchical Adversarial Decentralized Mean Field Control (HAD-MFC), where the upper level selects vulnerable agents as an NP-hard task and the lower level learns their worst-case adversarial policies via mean-field MARL. The two problems are coupled together, making HAD-MFC difficult to solve. To handle this, we first decouple the hierarchical process by Fenchel-Rockafellar transform, resulting a regularized mean-field Bellman operator for upper level that enables independent learning at each level, thus reducing computational complexity. We next reformulate the upper-level NP-hard problem as an MDP with dense rewards, allowing sequential identification of vulnerable agents via greedy and RL algorithms. This decomposition provably preserves the optimal solution. Experiments show our method effectively identifies more vulnerable agents in large-scale MARL and the rule-based system, fooling system into worse failures, and reveals the vulnerability of each agent in large systems. Code available at https://github.com/Waken-dream/VAI
